title: Attitudes of Students from Special Assistance Plan Schools towards Inclusivity
what_it_is: Attitudes of Students from Special Assistance Plan Schools towards Inclusivity

sections.label: SAP schools established 1979
sections.summary: Falling Chinese-medium school enrolment led the Government to establish SAP schools in 1979 to preserve Chinese-medium ethos and culture while using English as instruction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Recognising this, parents started sending their children to English schools and as a result, enrolment for Chinese-medium schools fell drastically in the 1970s and 1980s.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Hence, in 1979, the Government established SAP schools, to preserve the ethos of Chinese-medium schools and promote the learning of the language and its culture, while still using English as the primary language of instruction.

sections.label: SAP student attitudes study
sections.summary: A 2018 study found no difference in attitudes of Secondary school students in SAP and non-SAP schools towards people from different backgrounds and cultures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: A 2018 study found that there is no difference in the attitudes of Secondary school students in SAP and non-SAP schools towards people from different backgrounds and cultures.

sections.label: Malay programmes in SAP schools
sections.summary: Students can learn Malay or Bahasa Indonesia as a third language, and seven of 11 SAP Secondary schools run the Malay Special Programme within school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For example, they can learn Malay language or Bahasa Indonesia as a third language at the MOE Language Centre or take up the Malay Special Programme at the Zonal Centre or within the school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, seven out of 11 SAP Secondary schools implement their Malay Special Programme within the school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Furthermore, we have made Conversational Malay available in almost all SAP schools.

sections.label: Different schools in education landscape
sections.summary: Singapore is multi-racial and respects each community's language, customs and culture, so different kinds of schools all exist in the education landscape.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have majority of one community but we have decided we shall be a multi-racial country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But having done that, let us make sure we respect the fact that every community also values their own language, customs, culture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is why within our education system, different kinds of schools – from SAP schools to clan-based, church-based ones, specially-designated madrasah schools, the Umar Pulavar Tamil Language Centre – they all exist as part of our education landscape.

sections.label: SAP schools interaction downside
sections.summary: There is a place for all these schools, but SAP schools have a downside of fewer opportunities to interact with members of other races.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Therefore, there is a place for all these schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, within SAP schools, there is a downside – as the Member mentioned – which is that there are less opportunities to interact with members of other races.

sections.label: Conversational Malay in SAP schools
sections.summary: After visiting several SAP schools, the speaker is glad and amazed at their efforts to teach Conversational Malay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Visiting several SAP schools, I am actually quite glad and amazed at the efforts they have taken to teach Conversational Malay.
